correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the forest-extension identity by multigraph contraction and Laplacian determinant; for bounded opposite-endpoint test sets it bounds repeated-vertex candidate tuples as O(n^{k-1/2}), while matched tuples have exact inclusion probability (2/n)^k. This yields independent Poisson mixed factorial moments, local tightness, and vague convergence. A unique minimum-sum limiting atom has density 2 exp(-(x+y)^2), giving the independent Rayleigh-type deficit and uniform endpoint share by a Jacobian change. Finite checks exactly verify the inputs but are not used to claim infinite-dimensional certification.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The stated claim is a joint vague point-process convergence plus an explicitly marked extremal law. Fixed-forest inclusion does not alone state its limit; increasing-tree maximum span does not imply Cayley-tree limits because underlying probabilities differ. One-dimensional expectations or prefix counts do not determine the two-dimensional process. A hidden general theorem might still imply this as a special case, which is identified as residual risk.

originality.rationale: The fixed-order maximum span and full two-dimensional near-opposite-endpoint point-process statement were compared by implication with accessible full-text studies of (i) forest containment, (ii) numeric-label edge-weight extrema for increasing trees, (iii) length sums and optimized length in uniformly labelled trees, and (iv) prefix uncovering and two-tree overlaps. The same-weight, different-distribution increasing-tree paper is the closest and does not imply an all-Cayley-tree planar Poisson point process. No direct covered statement was found in the searched literature. A broader, as-yet-unidentified sparse-edge Poisson theorem remains a bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A broadly formulated but unlocated determinantal or sparse-edge Poisson theorem may already imply the specific endpoint process as a special case.
Unindexed literature concerning random-tree label bandwidth may contain an equivalent statement.
The preprint date of a historical source is not assumed to be its earliest public release.

value.rationale: The maximum span in a fixed label order is a natural null-model statistic for long-range links and dependency lengths in randomly labelled trees; unlike a single expected edge length, its extreme-event scale and endpoint geography quantify two simultaneously important aspects of a long-range link. The marked Poisson limit gives a complete tail law plus a genuinely independent endpoint-split distribution, useful for higher-order extremal statistics. The result concerns a natural full extreme, not an arbitrary numerically selected slice.
